testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you start an engine, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with your vehicle.

questions.question: Which rule about turn signals is NOT good?

options.text: Signal early. Signal before you turn or change lanes.
Signal the whole time. Keep signaling until your turn or lane change is done.
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, you don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, you don't need to signal.
questions.explanation: You should signal before every turn or lane change, signal while you are turning or changing lanes, and turn off your signal when you finish your move. Always signal, even if no one seems to be nearby.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times, then hold down the brake pedal.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can every time you slow down or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS. When ABS works correctly, it automatically prevents the brakes from locking up.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil.
questions.explanation: Brake linings should not be loose, wet with oil or grease, or too thin.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens most often when:

options.text: A vehicle is going faster than 60 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely when you drive on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tread. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Spread the weight evenly over the axles.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread the weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Your cargo must be balanced properly. Too much weight on one axle can damage it and make steering hard. Too little weight can cause poor traction and handling problems.

questions.question: When you check your tires, what should you NOT find?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires of different sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tire sizes should match.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
Is not something drivers need to worry about.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: Maximum axle weight is often set by a bridge formula. This formula allows less weight for axles that are close together.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from when you realize you need to brake until you actually hit the brakes
The distance you travel from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance you travel from when you see a hazard until you realize you need to brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from when you realize you need to brake until you actually hit the brakes
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels between the moment you decide to brake and the moment your foot hits the brake pedal.

questions.question: What should a safety belt do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Lock securely into place.
questions.explanation: When you check your vehicle, make sure the safety belt is firmly attached, adjusts properly, locks securely, and has no rips or tears.

questions.question: After you secure cargo on a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check the cargo again.
You should not let others look at the cargo.
You should check the cargo every 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check the cargo every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start driving, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: What test must you pass to transport hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: What needs extra attention during a winter pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: In winter, pay special attention to coolant and antifreeze levels, heating and defrosting equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer fluid, tires and tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, handholds, steps, deck plates, radiator shutters, winterfront, and the exhaust system.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, what must you do?

options.text: You never have to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always wear a seat belt when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires a CDL to drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: A school bus
questions.explanation: Military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, and recreational vehicles are exempt from CDL requirements. A school bus is not exempt.

questions.question: What happens when weight is poorly balanced in a trailer?

options.text: It makes the vehicle hard to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes the vehicle hard to control.
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle unsafe to handle. Too much or too little weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Weight should be spread evenly from front to back and side to side, and positioned as low as possible.

questions.question: What happens when cargo is loaded incorrectly?
questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded and secured properly for safety. Improper loading can damage the vehicle, cause cargo to fall off during a crash or sudden stop, and lead to injury or death.

questions.question: What should you know about trains at railroad crossings?

options.text: You will hear every train that approaches.
You may not hear a train, even if it is coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if it is coming.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear an approaching train. The train operator may not sound the horn, or horns may not be allowed in that area. Noise inside your vehicle can also prevent you from hearing a train until it is very close.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from them.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, keep plenty of distance between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door to see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use their mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Show other drivers you are angry.
Warn other drivers you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers you are near.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others that you are there. Only use it when needed, since it can startle other drivers and cause danger.

questions.question: Aggressive driving means:

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with care for other drivers' safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating your vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for other drivers' rights or safety.

questions.question: If in an accident, which action is not recommended?

options.text: Move your vehicle to the side of the road if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the scene.
questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene is illegal and can result in losing your license.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on roads.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road beneath it is visible, so the surface may look wet instead of icy. Watch for black ice when roads look wet and temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: When other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a multilane road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane of a multilane road if your truck is slow because of a heavy load. Let other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It distracts your mind and hands.
A text message might upset you.
People like to read and may focus too much on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts your mind and hands.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts your mind from the road and takes at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: For a 40-foot long load, the minimum number of tie-downs needed is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four tie-downs.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. Always stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.question: If being tailgated while driving a large vehicle, do all of the following except:

options.text: Increase your distance from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If tailgated, increase your distance from the car ahead and avoid quick movements. Speeding up will not help—the other driver will just tailgate you faster. Do not flash your brake lights at them.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from the body?

options.text: More quickly if the person stays awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a fixed rate.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Drinking coffee or taking a cold shower will not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to wait for your body to remove the alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Speed up and slow down frequently.
Change your driving to match the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your driving to match the weather.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down to match conditions. Your vehicle will take longer to stop, so increase your distance from other cars. Avoid speeding up and slowing down often.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used on the rear tires.
Yes, if carrying a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not safe.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: Is it good to look far ahead while driving?

options.text: No, there is little you can do about things far ahead.
Yes, it helps you see dangers early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps you see dangers early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look ahead at least 12 to 15 seconds. This gives you time to spot hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: What is special about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They cannot be driven on interstates.
They need special care when driving.
They usually cannot cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need special care when driving.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and the load can shift while moving.

questions.question: What might you be asked to do in a CDL vehicle inspection test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you may need to check the engine oil level.

questions.question: Does talking on a hands-free phone while driving distract you?

options.text: No, it does not distract the driver.
Only if the driver is speaking.
Yes, it can distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can distract the driver.
questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than handheld phones, but they still distract you mentally. Any conversation takes your focus away from driving.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the air compressor from pumping.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the air compressor from pumping.
questions.explanation: The governor controls when the air compressor pumps air. It stops pumping when air pressure gets too high and starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What condition should leaf springs be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaves should not be broken.
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs have no missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.

questions.question: What does blocking a load do?

options.text: It is dangerous and should never be done.
It keeps the load from shifting.
It is only used with liquid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps the load from shifting.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from moving during transport.

questions.question: If you transport hazardous materials that need placards, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Get a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to transport materials that require placards.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding around.
questions.explanation: Block cargo to prevent it from sliding during driving. Cargo that shifts can make steering and handling harder for the driver.

questions.question: When transporting a load, you should check the cargo:

options.text: At the end of each day.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Check it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: If a worker is in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Keep driving at the posted speed limit.
Slow down below the posted speed limit.
Drive off the road on the grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down below the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: In work zones, follow posted speed limits. When workers are present, drive even slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.
Should be used in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle tip over more easily than cargo with a low center of gravity. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Check that spring brakes turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes engage.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not touch each other.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: If you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, you:

options.text: May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Can expect other drivers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. Turning too soon can cause your vehicle's left side to hit another vehicle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop shortly after to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.
